text: Find the change from £5.00 after spending £3.85.
hints: You paid £5.00 and spent £3.85. The change is how much is left over.
Work in pence: 500p take away 385p. First take away 300p, then 85p.
Count up from 3.85: +15p makes £4.00, then +£1.00 makes £5.00. Add the jumps: 15p + £1.00.

text: Write 3/10 as a decimal.
A film starts at 3.40 p.m. and lasts 2 hours 15 minutes. What time does it finish?
hints: Start at 3.40 p.m. Add the length of the film to find the finishing time.
Add the 2 hours first. Then add the 15 minutes. Remember there are 60 minutes in an hour.
Timeline: 3.40 ─ +2 hours → 5.40 ─ +15 min → ?

text: Write 14 using Roman numerals.
How many days are there in March and April together?
hints: You need the number of days in each of the two months, then add them.
March has 31 days. April has 30 days. Add them together.
31 + 30: add 30 + 30 first, then add the extra 1.

text: A pack of 6 pencils costs 90p. How much does one pencil cost?
hints: The 6 pencils cost 90p altogether. You want the price of just one.
Share the cost equally between the pencils: 90p ÷ 6.
Try 10p each: 6 × 10p = 60p. That is not enough. Try 15p each and check 6 × 15p.

text: Tom has £2. He spends 65p and 48p. How much change does he get?
hints: Tom starts with £2. He spends money twice. The change is what is left.
Add the two amounts he spends: 65p + 48p. Then take that from 200p.
65 + 48 = 113. Now count up from 113 to 200 in jumps.

text: Write the missing signs +, −, × or ÷ in place of ● and ▲.   15 ● 3 = 2 ▲ 3
unit: Work out the left side first. Try each sign between 15 and 3.
15 ÷ 3 = 5. Now find the sign that makes 2 ▲ 3 equal 5.
Check: 2 + 3 = 5, so the signs are ÷ and +.

text: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2?
Round 4872 to the nearest hundred.
A rectangle is 9cm long and 4cm wide. What is the distance all the way round it?
hints: The distance round a shape is the perimeter. A rectangle has 4 sides.
Opposite sides are equal: two sides of 9cm and two sides of 4cm. Add all four.
Draw it: 9 + 4 + 9 + 4. Or add 9 + 4 first, then double it.

text: Write this date in digits only. The fourteenth day of June two thousand and eighteen.
Add the even numbers between 11 and 17.
hints: Between 11 and 17 means 12, 13, 14, 15, 16. You only want the even ones.
The even numbers are 12, 14 and 16. Add them together.

text: If 1kg of apples costs £2, find the cost of (a) 100g (b) 200g.
List the first four multiples of 6.
A film starts at 6.45 p.m. and ends at 8.20 p.m. How long is the film?
hints: The film runs from 6.45 p.m. to 8.20 p.m. You need the time in between.
Count on to the next hour: 6.45 to 7.45 is 1 hour. Then 7.45 to 8.20 is how many minutes?
Timeline: 6.45 ─ +1 hour → 7.45 ─ +? min → 8.20
